title: Specialist Referral Terms by Practice Type — Primary Care Provider Assignment
content:
**Schedule of referral terms under the Primary Care Provider Assignment.**

**Terms**

(a) Where the practice type requires a referral for specialist care, an in-network specialist visit needs a referral from the member's active PCP.

(b) A referral is valid for the practice type's referral validity days from its issue date, and covers up to the practice type's single-referral visit ceiling, or, for a standing referral where the practice type allows standing referrals, up to its standing-referral visit ceiling.

(c) Services in the self-referral list never need a referral: family planning, behavioral health, women's health, routine vision and dental. The list is the same for every practice type.

(d) A referral never replaces a prior authorization where one is required.

(e) A referral is issued only on a Primary Care Provider Assignment in active status, as the assignment's status stands on the system record before the referral is issued.

(f) A referral issued by a PCP whose assignment has since ended stays valid until its own expiry.

**Schedule**

| Practice type | Referral required for a specialist | Referral validity days | Single-referral visit ceiling | Standing referrals allowed | Standing-referral visit ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Primary Care Provider | Yes | 180 | 6 | No | 0 |
| Pediatric Primary Care Provider | Yes | 180 | 6 | No | 0 |
| OB/GYN Primary Care Provider | No | 180 | 6 | No | 0 |
| Federally Qualified Health Center Home | Yes | 180 | 6 | No | 0 |
| Patient-Centered Medical Home Practice | Yes | 365 | 12 | Yes | 24 |
| Specialist Serving as PCP | No | 365 | 12 | Yes | 36 |
| Health Home Lead Provider | Yes | 365 | 12 | Yes | 24 |

A standing-referral visit ceiling of 0 marks a practice type that does not allow standing referrals.

**Reading the schedule (hypothetical members)**

- A member assigned to a Standard Primary Care Provider who is going to an in-network cardiologist needs a referral from the active PCP; one referral covers up to 6 visits within 180 days of its issue date.
- A member assigned to an OB/GYN Primary Care Provider does not need a referral for an in-network specialist visit.
- A member assigned to a Pediatric Primary Care Provider may go to a routine vision visit without a referral.
- A member whose specialist procedure needs a prior authorization still needs that authorization even when holding a referral.
- A member who changed PCP keeps using an unexpired referral issued by the former PCP until the referral's own expiry.
